chapter.heading: The Just Judgment of the WickedTo the Chief Musician. Set to “Do Not Destroy.” A Michtam of David.
chapter.v:
Do you
indeed speak righteousness, you silent ones?Do you judge uprightly, you sons of men? [Ps. 58:2]

No, in
heart you work wickedness;You weigh out the violence of your hands in the earth.

The wicked
are estranged from the womb;They go astray as soon as they are born, speaking lies. [Is. 5:26] [Job 31:14 c Is. 13:6; Jer. 9:9; Hos. 9:7; Luke 19:44]

Their poison
is like the poison of a serpent;They are like the deaf cobra that stops its ear, [Is. 24:22]

Which will
not heed the voice of charmers,Charming ever so skillfully. [Jer. 51:20]

Break their
teeth in their mouth, O God!Break out the fangs of the young lions, O Lord! [Is. 9:17 i 2 Kin. 17:6; Jer. 34:22]

Let them
flow away as waters which run continually;When he bends his bow,Let his arrows be as if cut in pieces. [Gen. 50:20; Mic. 4:11, 12; Acts]

Let them
be like a snail which melts away as it goes,Like a stillborn child of a woman, that they may not see the sun. [2 Kin. 19:10]

Before your
pots can feel the burning thorns,He shall take them away as with a whirlwind,As in His living and burning wrath. [Gen. 10:10; Amos 6:2 m 2 Chr. 35:20 n 2 Kin. 16:9]

The righteous
shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance;He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked,

So that
men will say,“Surely there is a reward for the righteous;Surely He is God who judges in the earth.”
